title: Geo-fenced capacity fabric with soft isolation and graceful evacuation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need predictable throughput and strong data residency guarantees for regional/multi-zone dedicated fleets. Current placement is coarse-grained: it does not express soft isolation tiers, tiered evictions, or time-bounded evacuation windows, which causes hard failovers and pricey overprovisioning.

Goal: Implement a geo-fenced capacity fabric that lets admins declare residency boundaries and soft isolation tiers per dedicated pool; provide autoscaling policies that include buffer credits and pre-warm windows; and add graceful evacuation controls that preserve throughput for prioritized tenants during zone failures while respecting residency constraints. The solution should minimize cross-residency spillover and give measurable SLOs for throughput preservation and eviction rates.

Scope: This ticket covers the allocator and policy primitives, autoscale buffer accounting, an evacuation orchestrator for soft drains, and telemetry hooks (per-tenant throughput preservation metrics). It does NOT include UI work for the Console (separate PM ticket).

Key trade-offs being evaluated:
- Strict residency vs usable throughput: allow explicit escrow for short spillover vs enforcing hard locks that waste capacity.
- Evacuation latency vs throughput preservation: faster full-evacuations free capacity sooner but cause larger customer impact.
- Complexity of autoscale buffers: per-tenant buffer credits improve fairness but increase orchestration state and billing complexity.

Deliverables: allocator changes, policy schema + migration, autoscale buffer accounting, evacuation orchestrator service (beta), integration tests + simulator, runbook for failover and postmortem instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema accepts 'residency_scope' (region|multi-region|sovereign) and 'isolation_tier' (soft|strong) per pool
Allocator can reserve 'evacuation_escrow' capacity and honor residency flags during simulated zone loss
Autoscale supports buffer credits; default config preserves 95% of committed throughput under single-zone outage in simulations
Evacuation orchestrator exposes a graded eviction plan (tiered windows) and can target specific tenant slices for prioritized preservation
End-to-end test: simulated zone failure shows <5% increased 95th percentile latency for preserved tenants and no cross-residency state leakage
Monitoring: new metrics for 'throughput_preservation_ratio', 'evacuation_progress', and 'spillover_tokens' available in Console telemetry
technical_notes: Allocator: extend slot allocator with 'residency_scope' and 'isolation_tier' attributes; prefer same-region placement and allow short-term escrow with explicit TTL
Autoscale: introduce 'buffer_credits' per pool that are consumed on failover; credits are replenished by warm-up signals and policy rules
Evacuation: orchestrator will perform staggered draining windows (GracePeriodSmall=30s, GracePeriodLarge=5m) and a tenant-prioritization pass using SLA weights
KV cache locality: when spillover occurs, create read-only KV-cache shadow copies with strict residency tags to prevent leakage across sovereign boundaries
Fallback strategy: when residency prevents cross-region spill, trigger defined fallback models (lower tier quantized variants) in the same residency zone
Testing: we added a simulator that runs 10k synthetic requests across 100 tenants to validate throughput preservation under 1- and 2-zone loss scenarios
